lines.japanese: 月曜日の朝はいつもよりひとが無口に感じる。
lines.english: People always seemed quieter on Monday mornings.

lines.japanese: 別にそれは親しいひとの話じゃなくて、僕の知らないひとの僕の知らない世界での話だ。
lines.english: I did not mean anyone close to me. I meant strangers, living lives unknown to me in worlds of their own.

lines.japanese: もう三年も同じ電車で通ってると、自然と見かける回数が多いひとも増えてくる。そんなひとたちは一人でむっつりとつり革を握って、たまに席が空けばそこに座って、疲れたように頭をもたげている。
lines.english: After three years of commuting on the same train, one naturally accumulated familiar faces. These people stood alone and dour, gripping the straps. When a seat opened, they sank into it and tipped their heads back wearily.

lines.japanese: 彼らの声なんて聞いたこともないけど、月曜日は心の中で唇を結ぶ。そんな空気を感じるのが週の始めってやつだ。
lines.english: I had never heard their voices, yet on Mondays I could feel them pressing their lips together inside their hearts. That atmosphere was what the beginning of a week meant.

lines.japanese: 「やなぎはらー、やなぎはらー」
lines.english: “Yanagihara. Yanagihara.”

lines.japanese: 「終点ー、柳木原です。お忘れ物ないようご注意ください」
lines.english: “This train terminates at Yanagihara. Please take care not to leave any belongings behind.”

lines.japanese: 柳木原の駅構内ではビラ配りなどの行為は禁止されている。ただ駅から一歩出れば、オシャレな美容院や、ニュースで名前を知った金融会社や、全国チェーンの焼肉屋などのチラシが押しつけられる。
lines.english: Distributing flyers was prohibited inside Yanagihara Station. One step beyond its doors, however, and people thrust advertisements at you for fashionable salons, financial companies whose names I knew from the news, and nationwide chains of barbecue restaurants.

lines.japanese: こういうのはそのお店のひとや社員さんがやってるんだろうか。冬の寒い日は特に大変だろうけど、ご苦労なことだ。
lines.english: Did the people from those shops and companies hand the flyers out themselves? It must be especially hard on cold winter days. What a thankless job.

lines.japanese: かといって、僕だって必要のないチラシを受けとって、結局扱いに困って、ゴミ箱に捨てるような真似はめんどくさい。他の大多数のひとと同じく顔を真正面に向けて、伸びてくる手をやり過ごした。
lines.english: Even so, accepting a flyer I did not need, wondering what to do with it, and ultimately throwing it away was too much trouble. Like the vast majority of pedestrians, I fixed my gaze directly ahead and let the outstretched hands pass me by.

lines.japanese: 「おねがいしま、あ、すみませっ、あっ、おねがいしまっす」
lines.english: “P-please—oh, sorry! Ah—please!”

lines.japanese: そんな中、明らかに慣れない手つきで、頭を下げるというよりも、背中を丸めながら配っている女の子がいた。出したビラが時折ひとに当たって、振りかえった男性から舌打ちを浴びせられる。
lines.english: Among them was a girl whose clumsy motions plainly betrayed her inexperience. Rather than bowing, she hunched her back as she offered the papers. Now and then a flyer struck somebody, earning her an irritated click of the tongue when the man turned around.

lines.japanese: 明らかにビラ配りの作業を好んでやるタイプではなかった。きっと飲食店かなにかのアルバイトに応募して、最初に通らされる新人教育の一環を、流されるままに受けいれてしまったんだろう。
lines.english: She was clearly not the sort to volunteer for handing out flyers. She had probably applied for a job at a restaurant or somewhere, then meekly gone along with this first rite of training for new hires.

lines.japanese: 「あ、すみませっ」
lines.english: “Oh—sorry!”

lines.japanese: そうだ。そういえば、僕は焼肉屋に行ったことがない。訪れる機会はないかもしれないけど、値段設定だけ知っておくのも悪くない。
lines.english: Come to think of it, I had never visited a barbecue restaurant. I might never have occasion to enter one, but there was no harm in learning what they charged.

lines.japanese: 僕は差しだされた割引券付きのビラを、擦れちがいざまに受けとった。
lines.english: As I passed, I accepted the proffered flyer and its attached coupon.

lines.japanese: 「あっ、ありがとございまっす」
lines.english: “Oh! Thank you very much!”

lines.japanese: 黒い三角巾をした彼女は、丸めた背中をさらに折りまげて、僕に頭を下げた。つられた次のひとが手を出したから、慌てて２、３歩小走りに追いかけてビラを渡していた。
lines.english: The girl in the black triangular kerchief folded her already rounded back even farther in a bow. Inspired by my example, the next passerby extended a hand; she hurried after him for two or three little steps and delivered a flyer.

lines.japanese: 内容を見てみると、３１５０円以上の食事をされたお客様にはタン塩が半額と書いてある。紙幣を三枚出さなくちゃ使えない割引券。僕にはあまり縁がなさそうだ。
lines.english: It promised half-price salted beef tongue to customers spending at least 3,150 yen. A discount coupon you could not even use without taking out three banknotes. It was unlikely ever to concern me.

lines.japanese: だけど僕が使わないことは彼女の責任じゃない。
lines.english: But the fact that I would not use it was hardly her fault.

lines.japanese: 僕も焼肉屋の金額設定を知ることが出来たし、たまにはチラシを受けとってみるのもいいかもしれない。誰にも迷惑はかからないからね。
lines.english: I had learned what a barbecue restaurant cost, and perhaps accepting a flyer now and then was no bad thing. It harmed nobody.

lines.japanese: あ。
lines.english: Ah.

lines.japanese: いつもより心持ち早く歩いていた僕は、一本前の電車で降りた一群に追いついた。
lines.english: Walking a little faster than usual, I caught up with the crowd that had disembarked from the previous train.

lines.japanese: その中に見知った生徒が一人。僕はその姿を目で追ってみる。
lines.english: Among them was a student I knew. I followed her with my eyes.

lines.japanese: 今日は友人たちに出会わなかったのか一人みたいだ。ちょうどいい、土曜日の話がしたかったんだ。僕はちょっと小走りにその背中を追いかけた。
lines.english: Apparently she had not encountered her friends today and was alone. Perfect. I had wanted to speak about Saturday. I broke into a little trot after her.

lines.japanese: そういえば前にこの場所で彼女を見かけたときは、向こうから挨拶してくれたんだ。僕も彼女のように元気よくやってみよう。
lines.english: The last time I saw her here, she had greeted me first. I would try to be just as cheerful.

lines.japanese: さすがに大声を出すのは恥ずかしいけど、ちょっとびっくりさせるくらいはやってみよう。僕は小さく息を吸いこんだ。
lines.english: I was too embarrassed to shout, of course, but I might startle her a little. I drew a small breath.

lines.japanese: 「ちーっす、渡来さん！」
lines.english: “Mornin’, Watarai!”

lines.japanese: 口をすぼめるようにして、肩越しに声をかけた。横で縛った二つの髪束がふわりと舞って――
lines.english: Pursing my lips, I called over her shoulder. The two bunches of hair tied at either side floated lightly—

lines.japanese: 「へえー」
lines.english: “Oh, really?”

lines.japanese: ……あれっ。
lines.english: ...What?

lines.japanese: 彼女の口から出てきた言葉は、挨拶でも、それに準ずる言葉でもなく、相槌をうつような一言だった。
lines.english: The words from her lips were neither a greeting nor anything resembling one, but the vague acknowledgment offered in the middle of a conversation.

lines.japanese: 歩道橋の下で、車のクラクションの大きな音がした。渡来さんに目をとられて見えなかったけど、きっと朝の交差点は、混雑しているに違いない。
lines.english: A horn blared beneath the pedestrian bridge. I was too preoccupied with Watarai to see what had happened, but the morning intersection must have been congested.

lines.japanese: 「おはよう」
lines.english: “Good morning.”

lines.japanese: すぐに、いつもの柔和な微笑みが返ってきた。僕はほっと胸を撫で下ろす。
lines.english: Her usual mild smile followed at once. I breathed a sigh of relief.

lines.japanese: 僕は、少し小走りに隣に並んで、土曜日の話題を切りだそうとした。
lines.english: I hurried the last few steps to her side and tried to broach the subject of Saturday.

lines.japanese: が、挨拶を口にしたあとの彼女は、歩速を緩めるどころか、つかつかと進んで一気に歩道橋の向こう側へと突きすすんでいく。
lines.english: But once she had delivered her greeting, she did not slow. She strode briskly onward and swept across the pedestrian bridge.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あれっ。渡来さん待ってよ」
lines.english: “W-wait, Watarai.”

lines.japanese: 「ん、どしたの」
lines.english: “Hm? What is it?”

lines.japanese: 彼女の後ろ姿に向かって呼びかけたけど、横顔すら見えない。もしかして急いでるのかな。
lines.english: I called to her back, but could not see even her profile. Could she be in a hurry?

lines.japanese: 「あのさ、ちょっといいかな」
lines.english: “Um... Do you have a moment?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、いい」
lines.english: “Yes. That’s fine.”

lines.japanese: いいってどういうことだろう。彼女はもう下り階段にかかっていた。その直角の曲がり際、横顔だけかろうじて見えた。
lines.english: What did she mean by fine? She had already reached the descending stairs. As she turned the right-angled corner, I caught the barest glimpse of her profile.

lines.japanese: 「あのさ、あのさ渡来さん」
lines.english: “Listen—Watarai, listen.”

lines.japanese: 「ん、話があるなら歩きながら聞くよ」
lines.english: “If you have something to say, I’ll listen while we walk.”

lines.japanese: 「あれ、もしかして急いでるのかな」
lines.english: “Are you in a hurry?”

lines.japanese: 「ん、そうでもない」
lines.english: “Mmm. Not particularly.”

lines.japanese: 「はは、わ、渡来さん、足速いんだね」
lines.english: “Ha ha. Y-you walk very quickly.”

lines.japanese: 「んー、そかー」
lines.english: “Mm. Guess so.”

lines.japanese: 「あのね、土曜日のことなんだけどさ」
lines.english: “It’s about Saturday...”
“Ah.”

lines.japanese: そこで渡来さんが急に立ちどまった。僕は追いこしざま、ようやく彼女の顔と向き合った。
lines.english: Watarai stopped abruptly. I overshot her and at last found myself facing her.

lines.japanese: 「渡来さん、おはよう……」
lines.english: “Good morning, Watarai...”

lines.japanese: 「岡村ー！　おはよーっ！」
lines.english: “Okamura! Good morning!”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんが、僕の後ろ目掛けて大きな声を飛ばした。振りかえると、どこかで見たことのある二人組の女の子の姿が見える。
lines.english: Watarai shouted over my shoulder. When I turned, I saw a pair of girls I vaguely recognized.

lines.japanese: 渡来さんは僕の脇をすり抜けていくと、その二人の肩を飛びつくように抱えこんだ。
lines.english: Watarai slipped past me and flung her arms around their shoulders.

lines.japanese: 「岡村ー、この前貸したＣＤ持ってきてない？　急に聞きたくなっちゃったんだよね」
lines.english: “Okamura, did you bring that CD I lent you? I suddenly feel like listening to it again.”

lines.japanese: 「は？　だってなんか、しばらく聞かないからっつってなかったっけ？」
lines.english: “Huh? Didn’t you say you wouldn’t need it for a while?”

lines.japanese: 「んー、急に聞きたくなったんだから仕方ない。でも、ないなら諦めるかあ」
lines.english: “Mmm. I suddenly want it, so it can’t be helped. But if you don’t have it, I suppose I’ll give up.”

lines.japanese: 「ん、あー……あ、んじゃさ！　そだ、アレだろ例の。そろそろ打ちあわせしちゃう系？」
lines.english: “Mm... Oh! Hey, right, that thing! Are we gonna start planning it soon, or what?”

lines.japanese: 「そそ、分かってんじゃん。ちょうどその時期だと思ってたんだよね」
lines.english: “Yeah, yeah! See, you get it. I was just thinking it was about time.”

lines.japanese: 「あー、でしょでしょ！？　じゃ、急いで教室行かないと！」
lines.english: “Right? Right?! Then we’d better hurry to the classroom!”

lines.japanese: 「あははっ」
lines.english: “Ahaha!”

lines.japanese: 渡来さんの声は、その周りの女の子たちの声に掻きけされて聞こえにくかったけど、どうやら友達と大事な話があるみたいだ。
lines.english: The voices of the girls around her nearly drowned out Watarai’s, but apparently she had important business to discuss with her friends.

lines.japanese: 土曜日の話をしたかったけど、大事な用事があるんじゃ仕方ない。彼女は最初からとても急いでたし、きっとよほどのことがあるんだろう。邪魔をしたら申しわけない。そう、それだ。
lines.english: I had wanted to speak about Saturday, but there was no helping it if she had important business. She had been hurrying from the beginning. The matter must be terribly urgent. It would be wrong to interfere. Yes. That was it.

lines.japanese: 僕がその場から歩きはじめたときには、もう三人の姿は見えなくなっていた。昇降口までは、まだまだ距離がありそうだ。
lines.english: By the time I began walking again, the three of them had vanished. The school entrance still appeared some distance away.

lines.japanese: 昇降口まであと少しというところでクラスメイトの後姿を見かけた。
lines.english: Just before I reached it, I spotted the back of a classmate.

lines.japanese: 彼女の大きな声が頭の中に浮かんだけど、僕は声をかけることにした。
lines.english: Her loud voice sounded in my memory, but I decided to call to her.

lines.japanese: 「高内さん」
lines.english: “Takauchi.”

lines.japanese: 「んー？」
lines.english: “Hmm?”

lines.japanese: 「え？　羽田？」
lines.english: “What? Haneda?”

lines.japanese: 「はは……おはよう」
lines.english: “Ha ha... Good morning.”

lines.japanese: 「え、何？　なんだ、なんか用？」
lines.english: “What? What is it? You need something?”

lines.japanese: 高内さんは僕の顔を見ると眉をひそめた。月曜日は誰でも口をつぐむ日だから気持ちは分かる。
lines.english: Takauchi frowned when she saw my face. Monday was the day everyone closed their mouths, so I understood how she felt.

lines.japanese: 「なんだよ、何かあるなら早く言えって」
lines.english: “Well? If you want something, spit it out.”

lines.japanese: 彼女は靴を履きかえながら急かすように言った。本当は挨拶をしようと思っただけなんだけど、なにか話した方がいいのかな。
lines.english: She hurried me as she changed her shoes. I had only meant to say good morning, but perhaps I ought to find something to discuss.

lines.japanese: 「あの、卒業文集だけど……作業の方、どうかな」
lines.english: “Um... How is your part of the graduation anthology coming?”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 「何ソレ。なんか私ら信用されてないみたいなんだけど」
lines.english: “What’s that supposed to mean? Sounds like you don’t trust us.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことないよ。ただ、最後は足並みを揃えなくちゃいけないから、今の状況を確認しておこうと思っただけなんだ」
lines.english: “Not at all. But we’ll have to bring every part together at the end, so I thought I should check where things stand.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　なんでおまえ急にやる気出してんの？」
lines.english: “Huh? Since when are you so fired up about this?”

lines.japanese: 「急にってわけじゃないけど、あんまり時間もないからと思って……」
lines.english: “It isn’t sudden. We don’t have much time left, so I thought...”

lines.japanese: 「なんだよ、はっきり言えよ」
lines.english: “What? Just say what you mean.”

lines.japanese: 段々と彼女の声が大きくなってきたので、僕の声は吸いこまれるように尻すぼみになってしまった。それを見た高内さんの足が地面を叩く。
lines.english: Her voice grew steadily louder, and mine dwindled as though being swallowed. At the sight, Takauchi stamped one foot.

lines.japanese: 「あー、分かったよ。委員長様には迷惑かけないようにいたしますんで、あんたは自分の作業を頑張ってくれる？」
lines.english: “Fine, I get it. We’ll make sure not to inconvenience His Highness the Class President, so why don’t you concentrate on your own work?”

lines.japanese: 「う、うん」
lines.english: “Y-yes.”

lines.japanese: 「これでいいよな？　だからさー、ぶっちゃけオメ、大した用がないなら話しかけ……」
lines.english: “Satisfied? So, seriously, if you don’t actually need anything, don’t come talking to—”

lines.japanese: そこまで言って彼女は周囲を見渡した。僕もつられて首をぐるんと回してみたら、クラスの女子が僕たちを見て口笛を鳴らした。
lines.english: She broke off and glanced around. I swung my head around too and saw one of the girls in our class watching us and whistling.

lines.japanese: 彼女がどうして口笛を鳴らしたのかは分からなかったけど、正面からは高内さんの舌打ちの音が聞こえてきた。
lines.english: I did not understand why she had whistled, but from directly before me came the click of Takauchi’s tongue.

lines.japanese: 「超ウゼー……」
lines.english: “God, this is so annoying...”

lines.japanese: 「え、何が？」
lines.english: “What is?”

lines.japanese: 「あのさ、もう話済んだよな？　じゃあ私もう行っていい？　いいよな？　もう行くぞ？」
lines.english: “Listen, we’re finished here, right? So can I go now? I can, right? I’m going.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、え、えっと」
どうしよう、別に怒ってるわけじゃないみたいだけど、話を続けた方がいいのかな。他に話題……なにか興味をひけそうな……。
lines.english: What should I do? She did not seem precisely angry, but perhaps I ought to continue the conversation. Another subject... something that might interest her...

lines.japanese: 「あのさ、焼肉っておいしいよね」
lines.english: “You know, barbecue is delicious, isn’t it?”

lines.japanese: 「は？　焼肉？　はあ、まあ」
lines.english: “Huh? Barbecue? Yeah, I guess.”

lines.japanese: 「高内さん、食べたことあるのかな」
lines.english: “Have you ever had it, Takauchi?”

lines.japanese: 「ああそりゃ、フツー焼肉くらい食ったことあンでしょ。で、なに？」
lines.english: “Well, yeah. Everyone’s had barbecue. So what?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いや、３千円以上食べると、タン塩が半額になる割引券があるんだ」
lines.english: “Oh, nothing. I have a coupon for half-price salted beef tongue if you spend at least three thousand yen.”

lines.japanese: 「へー」
lines.english: “Huh.”

lines.japanese: 「はあ、なに、作業が終わったら、羽田が焼肉奢ってくれんの」
lines.english: “What, so when the work’s finished, you’re treating us to barbecue?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いや、そういうわけじゃないんだけどさ」
lines.english: “Oh, no. I didn’t mean that.”

lines.japanese: 「悪い、後輩見つけたからもう行くわ」
lines.english: “Sorry. I see an underclassman I know. I’m out of here.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、また後でね」
lines.english: “All right. See you later.”

lines.japanese: 軽く手を振って見送ると、高内さんは他の女生徒に声をかけて行ってしまった。
lines.english: I gave her a small wave. Takauchi called to another girl and left.

lines.japanese: やっぱり声の大きなひととの会話はまだ慣れないみたいだ。僕は自分の声の小ささを恥じて、喉を何度かンンッと鳴らした。
lines.english: Apparently I was still unused to speaking with loud people. Ashamed of my own quiet voice, I cleared my throat several times.

lines.japanese: 教室に入ってすぐに渡来さんの姿を探してみた。だけど彼女は僕の席から離れた場所で、女の子たちと盛りあがっていた。
lines.english: The moment I entered the classroom, I looked for Watarai. She was some distance from my seat, however, surrounded by girls and deep in lively conversation.

lines.japanese: いま話すのは無理みたいだ。あとで休憩時間に声をかけてみよう。
lines.english: Speaking to her now seemed impossible. I would approach her during a break.

lines.japanese: 教室の中には半分くらいの生徒。今日は少し来るのが早かったみたいだ。僕は窓際の席を目指して、教室の後ろをゆっくりと進んだ。
lines.english: The classroom was only half full. Apparently I had arrived a little early. I walked slowly along the back of the room toward my window seat.

lines.japanese: 自分の席に鞄を置くと、自分の席で本を読んでいる山科さんが目に入った。今朝通りかかったときに煙草屋の中をチェックしてみたけど、そのときに彼女の姿は見当たらなかった。
lines.english: After setting down my bag, I noticed Yamashina reading at her desk. I had glanced inside the tobacco shop on my way past that morning but had not seen her there.

lines.japanese: 僕の部屋に来たときは私服だったから、制服姿を見るとなんとなく緊張するな……別人みたいに見える。
lines.english: She had worn ordinary clothes when she visited my room. Seeing her in uniform made me strangely nervous... She looked almost like another person.

lines.japanese: ふと彼女が顔を後ろに向けた。自然、彼女を見ていた僕と目が合った。
lines.english: Suddenly she looked back. Since I had been watching her, our eyes met.

lines.japanese: 「おはよう、山科さん」
lines.english: “Good morning, Yamashina.”

lines.japanese: 彼女は体の内側で、手をぱくぱくと小さく動かした。僕も腰を下ろしながら、小さくぱくぱくを返しておいた。
lines.english: Close against her body, she opened and closed one hand in a tiny wave. As I sat, I returned the same little wave.

lines.japanese: それを見た山科さんは、くすりと上品に微笑んでくれた。僕と山科さんだけに通じる、秘密の挨拶。
lines.english: At the sight, Yamashina gave a soft, refined smile. It was a secret greeting understood by only the two of us.

lines.japanese: ざわめいた教室の中で、この挨拶なら声の小さい僕でも伝えることが出来る。
lines.english: Even with the classroom in an uproar, a greeting like this let somebody as soft-spoken as me make himself understood.

lines.japanese: それが嬉しかったのか、思わず笑いが漏れそうになった。でも僕は山科さんみたいに綺麗には笑えないから我慢しよう。
lines.english: The pleasure of it almost made me laugh aloud. But I could never laugh as beautifully as Yamashina, so I restrained myself.

lines.japanese: いいんだ、男の子は軽々しく笑うもんじゃない。なんてことを、どこかの侍が言ってた気がする。
lines.english: That was right. A boy ought not laugh too readily. I thought some samurai somewhere had said as much.

lines.japanese: さて、準備しようかな……。
lines.english: Well, then. I should get ready...

lines.japanese: 鞄から教科書を取りだしていたら、後ろ側の扉が開いた。
lines.english: As I took my textbooks from my bag, the rear door opened.

lines.japanese: 針生さんだ。意外……って言ったら失礼だけど、時間通り来るなんて珍しいな。
lines.english: It was Hariu. Perhaps it was rude to call it unexpected, but seeing him arrive on time was certainly unusual.

lines.japanese: 彼は自分の席まで進むとどすんと鞄を置いて、そこからペットボトルだけを取りだした。
lines.english: He walked to his desk, dropped his bag on it with a thud, and removed only a plastic bottle.

lines.japanese: あれ？　いつもならすぐ席について、目を閉じるか、首を回して教室内を見渡したりしてるのに、今日はどうしたんだろう。
lines.english: What? Ordinarily he sat at once and either closed his eyes or turned his head to survey the classroom. What was different today?

lines.japanese: まあでも、針生さんが来てくれたのは嬉しいことだ。今日は放課後の作業をお願いしよう。
lines.english: In any case, I was glad Hariu had come. I would ask for his help after school.

lines.japanese: そう思って鞄に意識を戻したら、横でぐびっと喉を鳴らす音がした。
lines.english: Just as I turned my attention back to my bag, a loud gulp sounded beside me.

lines.japanese: 「おい」
lines.english: “Hey.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: 針生さんが僕に話しかけてきた。針生さんの方から話しかけてくれるなんて珍しいけど、なんだろう。
lines.english: Hariu had addressed me. It was rare for him to begin a conversation. What could he want?

lines.japanese: 「あ、おはようございます。今日は早いんですね」
lines.english: “Oh, good morning. You’re early today.”

lines.japanese: 「ああ、おまえと話をしようと思ってなァ」
lines.english: “Yeah. Came to talk to you.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、おれと？」
lines.english: “What? To me?”

lines.japanese: 針生さんと話すこと自体が珍しいのに、僕と話すために早くきてくれた？
lines.english: Conversation with Hariu was unusual to begin with, yet he had come early specifically to speak to me?

lines.japanese: なんの話だろう、楽しみだ。僕は逸る気持ちを抑えて、針生さんの言葉を待った。
lines.english: What could the subject be? I suppressed my mounting excitement and waited for him to continue.

lines.japanese: 「ギャルゲーやってみた」
lines.english: “Tried that dating game.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ」
lines.english: “What?”

lines.japanese: ギャルゲー……って、前に僕が勧めたあのギャルゲーのこと……だよね。
lines.english: That dating game... He meant the one I had recommended before... surely.

lines.japanese: 「なかなかロックだった。ただどうしても担任の熱血女教師が俺になびかない──」
lines.english: “Pretty damn rock. But no matter what I do, the hot-blooded homeroom teacher won’t fall for me—”
“W-wait, wait!”

lines.japanese: 僕は慌てて針生さんの袖を引いた。彼は低いけどよく通る声をしてるから、ギャルゲーの話が教室中に聞こえてしまう。
lines.english: I hastily tugged Hariu’s sleeve. His voice was low but carried remarkably well. The entire classroom would hear us discussing dating games.

lines.japanese: 「ま、待ってください、それはなにも、こんなところじゃなくても」
lines.english: “P-please wait. We don’t have to discuss that here.”

lines.japanese: 「こんなところ？　意味分かんねえ」
lines.english: “Here? The hell’s that supposed to mean?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、あの、あんまりそういう話は人前でしない方がいいって、前に言われたことがあって……」
lines.english: “Um... Somebody once told me it was better not to discuss things like this in public...”

lines.japanese: 「なんだそりゃ。好きなモンを好きと言ってなにが悪いんだよ」
lines.english: “What kind of crap is that? What’s wrong with saying you like what you like?”

lines.japanese: 「え、それは……」
lines.english: “Well...”

lines.japanese: なんでだろう。そう言われると、言いかえせる理由を僕は持ってない。
lines.english: Why indeed? Put that way, I had no answer.

lines.japanese: 「でも渡来さんに聞かれたりするのは恥ずかしいですよ」
lines.english: “But I’d be embarrassed if Watarai heard us.”

lines.japanese: 「そうかあ？　まあ女は萌えとか分かんねえもんなァ、つまンねえ生き物」
lines.english: “Would you? Well, women don’t understand the appeal of fictional girls anyway. Boring creatures.”

lines.japanese: 「まあいいや。だったら俺と二人で萌えについて語ろうぜ。先達としてのおまえの意見が聞きたい」
lines.english: “Whatever. Then you and I can discuss what makes fictional girls appealing. I want the opinion of an old hand.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、それならいいですよ。なんでも聞いてください」
lines.english: “Oh. That would be fine. Ask me anything.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあたとえば、俺がプリムラに『お兄ちゃん』と呼ばれたときに感じるこの名状しがたい高揚感は、果たしてドーパミン由来の症状なのかフェニルエチルアミンによるものなのか、羽田、おまえはどう思う」
lines.english: “Then suppose Primula calls me ‘Big Brother.’ That indescribable rush I feel—is it a dopamine response, or the work of phenethylamine? What do you think, Haneda?”

lines.japanese: 「え、萌えについて語るってそういう方向性だったんですか」
lines.english: “What? Is that where you meant our discussion of cute-girl appeal to go?”

lines.japanese: 針生さんはまだもうひとつ萌えというものを理解できていないようだった。
lines.english: Hariu still did not entirely understand the concept.

lines.japanese: しばらく話していたら、盛りあがってきたところで担任の恩田先生が入ってきた。
lines.english: We had spoken for some time and were just becoming animated when our homeroom teacher, Ms. Onda, entered.

lines.japanese: 「ちっ、空気読めよ担任。羽田ァ、続きは一限目が終わってからだな」
lines.english: “Tch. Read the room, Teach. Haneda, we’ll continue after first period.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、はい」
lines.english: “Oh. Yes.”

lines.japanese: 針生さんはふらふらと自分の席に戻っていった。そうか、次の休み時間も話をしにきてくれるんだ。
lines.english: Hariu wandered back to his desk. So he would come speak to me again during the next break.

lines.japanese: 休み時間に盛りあがって、話が終わる前に先生が来るなんて滅多にないことだ。僕はつい手振りまで加えて解説してしまった。
lines.english: Rarely had a break-time conversation grown so lively that the teacher arrived before it ended. I had even found myself gesturing as I explained.

lines.japanese: 僕はまだ話の興奮が冷めずに、どきどきしていた。
lines.english: The excitement of the conversation had not yet subsided. My heart continued to race.

lines.japanese: 「委員長、朝の号令は」
lines.english: “Class President. The morning greeting.”

lines.japanese: 「あっ、すみません！」
lines.english: “Oh! I'm sorry!”

lines.japanese: 朝の習慣を忘れるくらい、興奮していた。
lines.english: I had been excited enough to forget our morning ritual.
